headline: Foundation models map multimodal biological data onto cell, protein, and tissue states
label: Foundation Models For Biological Data
summary: Pathology benchmarks, spatial proteomics models, and image-conditioned expression generators are emerging together in recent preprints and publications.
synthesis: The dominant thread is large pretrained or generative models that map heterogeneous measurements, including histopathology, microscopy, sequences, and clinical metadata, onto biological state representations. M3-Gen conditions a GAN on histopathology images and clinical metadata, using contrastive learning and attention to generate TCGA gene expression profiles with an interpretability focus. scMIR pretrains a vision-language model on 207,957 image-text pairs to unify morphological and biological semantics in single-cell microscopy. SPgen integrates sequences and annotations within a multi-modality foundation framework to predict proteome-wide spatial protein expression, while Spatium trains a protein language model on over 51 million cells across spatial proteomics platforms for panel-robust cell representations. A benchmark of 32 vision and vision-language models across TCGA, CPTAC, and out-of-domain tasks supplies comparative grounding. What is new is the output target: expression profiles generated from images, proteome-wide spatial prediction, and panel-robust cell representations.
